messages:
erin: heads-up — after the kernel selection + batching tweak last night we saw a sharp drop in prefix-cache hits for a small cohort. profiler snapshots attached inline.

mike: saw that in the dashboards too, hit rate from ~0.78 -> ~0.45 for the web-chat cohort. same request mix but different kernel path.

tess: do we have a diff of the cache key bytes before/after? could be ordering or subtle tokenization change.

erin: short dump from the edge tracer: 
```
# before (stable-key-v1 generation)
key = sha1(system_prompt + user_prompt + json(tool_args))
# after (kernel v2.3 path)
key = sha1(system_prompt + user_prompt + json(tool_args, sort_keys=True))
```
not the exact code but you get the idea — ordering changed in some tool payloads.

andre: notable: tokenizer labeled as "tokenizer-v5" on old infra, new kernel routes some requests through our fast token path which reports a different tokenizer id (tokenizer-v5-light). that changes tokenization for certain unicode sequences.

julia: wow, so two orthogonal deltas: JSON key ordering + tokenizer variant. combined effect could explain multiplicative hit loss.

erin: profiler snippet (simplified): 
```
2026-02-11T22:30:05Z kernel=v2.3 batch_size=8 cohort=web-chat cache_hit_rate=0.41 warmup_hits=0.10
2026-02-11T22:29:50Z kernel=v2.2 batch_size=8 cohort=web-chat cache_hit_rate=0.79 warmup_hits=0.47
```

mike: timestamps line up with the deploy. ci-bot shows the canary rolled at 22:28.

ci-bot: deploy: kernel/v2.3 -> canary (eng-runtime) by ryan at 2026-02-11T22:27:49Z.

tess: proposal: decouple stable cache signature from non-semantic tool arg ordering and tokenizer label. canonicalization rules: 1) normalize unicode NFKC, 2) canonical JSON for tool args (stable canonicalizer that preserves arrays order but sorts object keys), 3) include tokenizer fingerprint that is invariant across equivalent token implementations.

andre: how do we make a tokenizer fingerprint? maybe use a hash of the repr of the tokenizer pipeline (vocab hash + normalizer version + special-token map). that way light vs full tokenizers map to same fingerprint if they are compatible.

erin: yes — and for incompatible tokenizer variants we should treat them as distinct keys (fallback to full warmup). also suggested: include a short schema version for the system_prompt processing pipeline (we've had system prompt rewrite in a patch last month).

mike: another mitigation: add a transient warmup policy that prefetches top-k likely prefixes for request cohorts during rollout. should be cheap and decidable by cohort ID.

julia: can we compute expected cache coverage for prefetch? run cohort replay on a warmup runner for 30m and output top-100 prefixes.

tess: quick test run looks promising: replayed 50k requests, top-100 prefixes cover 62% of hits. prefetching those would restore most of the lost hit-rate for this cohort.

erin: action items I suggest: 
- short (owner: tess): implement stable-canonicalizer lib and run it in a small canary (prefix-only path) by EOD.
- medium (owner: andre): produce tokenizer-fingerprint spec and a migration map for tokenizers we consider equivalent.
- infra (owner: mike): enable cohort prefetch warmup for the canary rollout and throttle it to 5 QPS to limit cost.
- ops (owner: julia): roll kernel v2.3 -> rollback if canary doesn't regain >=0.7 cache hit for primary cohort within 2h.

andre: nit: canonicalizer must preserve tool arg array order (users rely on position), only sort object keys. also strip null/empty metadata fields by default to avoid noisy differences.

mike: I'll stub the prefetch job and hook it to the trace replay infra, linking results to the console heatmap so we can watch hit recovery live.

erin: good. small config note: prefer a low-entropy short field in the cache key for tokenizer fingerprint (e.g. "tfp:sha1(vocab|norm|spec)") not full blobs.

julia: will coordinate on SLO update and send an incident-style note if rollback is triggered.

mike: anyone object to an immediate canary rollback until stable-key library is in place?

tess: prefer keep canary rolling but with prefetch on and canonicalizer enabled on the prefix path only — less blast radius.

erin: consensus: keep canary w/ mitigations. doing canonicalizer + tokenizer fingerprint spec + prefetch. rollback if no improvement in 2h. I'll follow up with a short runbook and timeline.

ci-bot: reminder: perf-alert threshold breached for eng-runtime cohort=web-chat hit-rate < 0.5 at 2026-02-11T22:31:12Z.

andre: logging: add a small hist for "cache-signature-delta" that counts keys that changed due to ordering vs tokenizer mismatch. will help quantify.

julia: thanks all — please add short status updates as you make progress. :+1:
